dedupe_keys.name: geomagnetic storm effects on cathodic protection of the neuba ii and san martin gas pipelines argentina 2013 2018

description: This study by Patricia Larocca and Maria Alejandra Arecco of the Institute of Geodesy and Applied Geophysics, University of Buenos Aires, published in AIMS Geosciences in 2025, investigates how geomagnetic field fluctuations driven by solar activity affect cathodic protection on two major gas pipelines in Argentina: NEUBA II at mid latitude and San Martin Fueguino at high latitude. Coverage: anomalies in pipe-to-soil potential recorded at 38 monitoring points between 2013 and 2018, analysed against the Dst and Kp indices, sunspot number and the F10.7 cm solar radio flux. The authors add the second vertical derivative of the geomagnetic field to detect rapid, local variations, and find that even subtle changes in quiet periods can produce out-of-range protection records that compromise cathodic protection and may accelerate corrosion. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: two pipelines; the abstract was the part read, and the monitoring records are not described as released. The index thresholds and monitoring approach can set space weather hazard inputs for pipeline corrosion and exposure models. It relates to the New Zealand pipe-to-soil potential model and INTERMAGNET in the catalogue.
